posts.author: Turtle
posts.body:
Howdy! I am
not
a professional artist, so
I will not be doing requests
.
My focus is on creating free resources that will make it easier to create games that are more inclusive of lots of different kinds of humans. So the stuff I share will mainly be BIMPOC, queer, and disability rep.
Again, I am
not
a trained artist so you are more than welcome to touch-up, re-edit and by all means post better versions of my stuff. All I ask is that you link back to the specific image you found when you post it so folks will be able to use both versions if they want.
Other Diverse/Inclusive Resources:
Avery created adorable angel sprites with a wide range of skin tones that you can find
here
. (You will need to slice the image into two separate image files in order for it to fit the
character sprite-sheet requirements
, but if I could figure out how to do that you probably can too.)
There is also a wheelchair animated charset from Avery
here
.
HiddenOne has some diverse modern character sprites as well as some cane-using sprites
here
.
MarioLuigi34 (credited as SomeNewWork) has created some generator parts that include fat/pregnant body types
here
.
I wasn't seeing any busts or emote artwork anywhere (if y'all know of any please feel free to link them in this thread), so that's my first project. But first...
TERMS:
-You must own a licensed copy of RPG Maker MZ to use these and follow RMMZ licensing rules (unless an asset is specifcally labeled as an original work)
-You can use these in both Non-Commercial and Commercial games
-
You
may not
use these in adult (as in x-rated) or obscene games.
-
You may not use these for NFTs or AI training.
-You are free to edit and post, but you must include a link back to the asset you edited in your post.
-Credit Kadokawa and Turtle (unless an asset is marked as original work, then just credit Turtle)

How to Use Gradient Extension:
Locate the skin_grad file in your generator folder
Make a backup of skin_grad and save it in another folder just in case
Open a copy of skin_grad in Gimp
Extend the canvas height by 12 pixels (or 4 pixels per row)
Insert this image in the newly created empty space
Export the new file as a png
Not sure if this next step is necessary for gradients, but I then run files through
GlueIT
Rename the new file as skin_grad, and use it to replace the old one in your generator folder

Today we have my first stab at a full tilesheet. I wanted to set up the pride flags so you could put them in pretty much any part of the tile/tiles without needing to go in and slice it up. If you have a plug-in like VistuStella's Grid-Free Doodads, you'll only really need the top row. I don't have a plug-in like that, but I might cave one day. Who knows? Haha.
The flags in the top row are (from left to right):
1. Gay Pride
2. Neutrois Pride
3. Intersex Pride
4. Ace Pride (Asexual Pride)
5. Lesbian Pride
6. Transgender Pride
7. Enby Pride (Non-binary Pride)
8. Polysexual Pride
9. Pansexual Pride
10. Aromantic Pride
11. Bisexual Pride
12. Genderfluid Pride
13. Genderqueer Pride
14. Agender Pride
And I also made a little bouncy pride flag animation:
You can use these outside of RPG Maker MZ. See the first post in this thread for other terms that apply.
And now you're all set for Pride Month! Enjoy!

posts.author: Turtle
posts.body:
Since making sprites was so difficult, this time I tried generating a character that I could then alter the face into an emote face and bust set.
But the options for hair are incredibly limiting for one. I managed to get one sprite that if you squint at it hard enough kinda looks like it has dreads.
I settled for that, got it all dressed up in the same outfit that Actor 2-7 wears so I could take the face bit and just enlarge and extend it into a bust— and that's when I learned that the proportions of the art changes between the face and the bust. So that was a no-go.
Long story short, I basically had to recolor and redraw parts of Actor 2-7 so he could have a bust emote set. But on the plus side, his sprite, down sprite, and battler ARE buildable using the character generator.
So here's the first bust in his set:

Part of the reason that making more diverse characters with the default character generator is the lack of variation in textured hair, right? So I thought to myself, why don't I just make generator parts that folks can use for themselves.
And holy moly, that is a lot of work.
I just finished with generator parts for ONE hairstyle for the Kid section of the generator. I've got the same hairstyle part in progress for the "Female" and "Male" sections, but I'm honestly not sure I will complete it.
For the life of me, I could not figure out how to make a color mask file that the generator would recognize-- even when I made them the same yellow as the files in the default generator. So it is what it is.
NOTE:
Please backup your generator folder before making any changes to it
If you've added content to the Kid section of the generator, you may need to renumber the file names
The hairstyle will shift color on the face image, but NOT on the sprite
The hairstyle is a set of front hair and rear hair. If you don't use them both together (or with some other suitable part), it's going to look really weird.

Lately I've been digging more into the mechanics and UI/menu side of my game, so I haven't been making as many assets of the kind that belong in this thread.
But today I took a quick break to tackle something about the generator gradients that have been bugging me. The skin gradient in my generator is already a Frankenstein of the default gradient and a couple other community-made gradients, but all the darker skin-tone options either don't go as dark as I would like or they look super ashy. So this is my first attempt at making a skin gradient of any kind, but I tested them all out, and they definitely work.
How to Use:
Locate the skin_grad file in your generator folder
Make a backup of skin_grad and save it in another folder just in case
Open a copy of skin_grad in Gimp
Extend the canvas height by 12 pixels
Insert this image in the newly created empty space
Export the new file as a png
Not sure if this next step is necessary for gradients, but I then run files through
GlueIT
Rename the new file as skin_grad, and use it to replace the old one in your generator folder
Here's the gradient extension file:
